name: Customer Base Growth
description: Project how a customer base changes when acquisition and churn pull in opposite directions.
formula: Net monthly change = (Base x Acquisition Rate) - (Base x Churn Rate); Ending Base = Base + (Net x Months)
business_contexts: a streaming service tracking subscriber momentum after a price change
a gym chain modelling membership over the next year
a mobile carrier projecting its prepaid subscriber base
a subscription box company planning warehouse capacity
a digital bank forecasting active account growth
question_patterns: How many customers will the business have at the end of the period?
What is the ending customer base after the analysis period?
Where does the customer base land once acquisition and churn are netted out?
How large is the customer base at the end of the projection window?
solution_logic: Step 1: Monthly new customers = starting_customer_base x monthly_acquisition_rate
Step 2: Monthly churned customers = starting_customer_base x monthly_churn_rate
Step 3: Net monthly change = new customers - churned customers
Step 4: Ending base = starting base + (net monthly change x analysis_months)
key_insight: Growth is the gap between acquisition and churn. A large acquisition number means nothing if churn is close behind it.
common_mistakes: Reading the acquisition rate as growth and ignoring churn entirely
Treating churn as a fixed number of customers rather than a rate
Forgetting to multiply the net monthly change across the full period
framework_soundbite: Net growth is acquisition minus churn. If churn is close to acquisition, the bucket leaks as fast as it fills.
